title: adaptive-ingest-shaper-for-onprem-telemetry-to-protect-tenant-isolation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) customers occasionally experience telemetry ingestion storms from noisy tenants or misconfigured agents (esp. sidecars and edge collectors). These storms cause downstream pipeline lag, SLO breaches on latency dashboards, and noisy error spikes in the console. Existing tenant isolation is coarse (per-collector) and does not adapt to bursty patterns.

Goal: Implement an adaptive ingest shaper that sits at the on-prem/VPC collector ingress layer to enforce per-tenant isolation, protect shared pipelines, and preserve end-to-end tracing fidelity. The shaper must: enforce soft and hard limits per tenant, dynamically adjust batching and flush frequency based on load and latency SLOs, attach lightweight tracing hooks/trace-context-preservation headers, and emit metrics for downstream dashboards. It should work in both Dedicated and Private deployment models and be configurable via the existing collector config with sane defaults.

Scope: design + prototype + roll out to internal dogfood Dedicated clusters and 2 pilot customers. Exclude deep storage changes and long-term archival optimizations (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: Ingress shaper runs as an optional filter in the on-prem/VPC collector and can be toggled by config
Per-tenant soft limit prevents pipeline lag by buffering and adaptive batching; hard limit rejects excess data with clear 429-like telemetry responses
Trace context headers are preserved across shaper buffers and emitted as span tags in downstream traces
New metrics emitted: tenant_ingest_rate, tenant_buffer_latency_p95, tenant_rejects, shaper_backpressure_events
Dashboards updated to show top 50 tenants by buffer latency and rejects; alerts trigger before SLO breach
Load test (simulated noisy tenant) shows 80% reduction in downstream pipeline latency under same ingest volume
Configuration documented in Confluence and included in onprem upgrade notes
implementation_notes:
Design: lightweight Go filter inside the collector process using a token-bucket per tenant plus an adaptive batch window. When buffer latency approaches configured SLO (default 100ms p95), we shrink batch size and increase flush frequency. On sustained overload, we switch to probabilistic drop with exponential backoff per tenant and emit a reject event. Trace propagation: preserve W3C traceparent and tracestate headers in buffer meta and ensure the span ID is attached to outgoing events for downstream correlation. Persistence: short in-memory per-tenant ring buffer with configurable max memory; avoid local disk in first phase. Config knobs exposed: tenant_soft_rps, tenant_hard_rps, max_buffer_ms, batch_size_min, batch_size_max, grace_period_ms.

Trade-offs: in-memory ring buffers are simpler and lower latency but can lose data on collector restart. We accept eventual loss for the first rollout to prioritize SLO protection; durable buffering is a follow-up. Probabilistic dropping minimizes global impact but can affect a noisy tenant's observability; mitigation: provide tenant-level diagnostics and per-tenant SLA exemptions (allowed via enterprise config).
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy shaper behind feature flag in internal dogfood Dedicated cluster (1 week). 2) Run chaos tests and synthetic noisy-tenant load generator (locust-like) to validate metrics and dashboards (2 weeks). 3) Enable for two pilot customers (opt-in) with 48h monitoring and rollback window. 4) Gradual rollout to all Dedicated clusters with default conservative limits and template configs for Private customers. 5) Follow-up: durable buffer and policy-management UI in Console.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for token-bucket logic and adaptive window transitions.
- Integration tests with collector e2e harness to verify trace context preservation and emitted metrics.
- Load tests with variable tenant mix: single noisy tenant, 1000 small tenants, 10 medium tenants.
- Observability: new Grafana panel measuring tenant_buffer_latency_p95 and synthetic alert firing simulation.
- Security: confirm no trace headers are leaked to tenants across boundaries.
risks: Data loss on collector restarts (mitigated by documenting expectations and follow-up durable buffer work)
Config complexity for on-prem admins (mitigated by providing sane defaults and example profiles)
Unexpected interaction with existing batching in upstream pipelines (integration testing required)
Potential for false positive alerts during rollout (monitoring and alert tuning required)
